Sunrise Riding: First Light on Two Wheels

Sunrise rides are a secret pleasure known only to committed motorcyclists. The roads are empty, the air is fresh, and the light paints landscapes in colours you won't see at any other time. It requires an early alarm, but the rewards are exceptional.

East Coast Sunrises

Britain's east coast catches the first light:

  • Dunstanburgh Castle, Northumberland: The ruined castle silhouetted against a dawn sky over the North Sea is one of Britain's most photographed scenes. Ride the coastal B1339 to Craster and walk to the castle.
  • Robin Hood's Bay, Yorkshire: The fishing village tumbling down cliffs to the sea catches the dawn light beautifully. Ride the moorland roads early and arrive for sunrise.
  • Beachy Head, Sussex: The chalk cliffs glow pink and gold at dawn. The road is empty at 5am and the views are extraordinary.

Mountain Sunrises

  • Pen-y-Pass, Snowdonia: Dawn at the top of the Llanberis Pass, with Snowdon's shadow retreating across the valley, is special. The car park is empty at dawn — a rare occurrence.
  • Bealach na Bà summit: If you camp at Applecross, ride the pass at dawn. The sun rises behind the mountains and the views west are bathed in soft morning light.
  • Hartside Summit, A686: The eastern view catches sunrise over the North Pennines. In autumn, the valleys fill with mist and the sun lights the mist from above.

Advantages of Dawn Rides

  • Empty roads: At 5am, even popular biking roads are deserted. You have the road to yourself.
  • Wildlife: Dawn is the best time to spot deer, hares, and raptors. They're active at first light and less wary.
  • Light quality: The low sun creates long shadows, warm colours, and dramatic landscapes. Photographers call it the magic hour for good reason.
  • Temperature: Cool air is denser and the bike feels slightly more powerful. The crispness of a dawn ride is uniquely refreshing.
Dawn riding requires cold-weather preparation regardless of season. Summer mornings at altitude can be surprisingly cold — 5-8°C is common in the Scottish Highlands even in July. Layer up and warm up before riding. Cold muscles and stiff joints make for less controlled riding.

Sunrise Times (Approximate)

  • Midsummer (June): 4:30-5:00am in Scotland, 4:45-5:15am in southern England
  • Spring/Autumn equinox: 6:00-6:30am across the UK
  • Midwinter (December): 8:30-9:00am in Scotland, 8:00-8:15am in southern England

A sunrise ride costs you only an hour of sleep but gives you empty roads, extraordinary light, and memories that last far longer than the lie-in you sacrificed. keyTakeaways: East-facing coasts catch first light, with Dunstanburgh Castle and Robin Hood's Bay among the finest.
Dawn rides give empty roads, active wildlife, and the photographer's magic hour of long shadows and warm colour.
Mountain sunrises at Pen-y-Pass or Hartside can sit above valleys filled with autumn mist.

faq.q: What time do I need to set off for sunrise?
faq.a: It depends on the season. Midsummer sunrise is around 4:30 to 5am in Scotland and slightly later in southern England, so an early alarm is unavoidable. Around the equinoxes it is a more civilised 6 to 6:30am, and in midwinter it slips to 8am or later. Aim to reach your viewpoint 20 to 30 minutes before sunrise to settle and let your eyes adjust.

faq.q: Why ride at dawn rather than any other time?
faq.a: At first light even popular biking roads are deserted, giving you the tarmac to yourself. Wildlife such as deer and hares is active and less wary, so ride alert for animals on the road. The low sun creates long shadows and warm colours that photographers prize, and the crisp, dense morning air makes the whole experience uniquely refreshing.

faq.q: How cold does it get on a dawn ride?
faq.a: Colder than you expect, whatever the season. Summer mornings at altitude in the Scottish Highlands commonly sit at 5 to 8C even in July, and coastal dawns are chilly with the wind. Layer up, add thermal gloves if needed, and warm up gently before pressing on, because cold muscles and stiff joints reduce your control in the first miles.

faq.q: Where is best for a coastal sunrise?
faq.a: Britain's east coast catches the first light. Dunstanburgh Castle silhouetted against the North Sea is one of the country's most photographed dawn scenes, reached via the coastal roads to Craster and a short walk. Robin Hood's Bay in Yorkshire and the chalk of Beachy Head in Sussex are also superb, and all three are gloriously quiet at 5am.
